spaces.deleteText: Every note and file of the space goes into the trash, and the space disappears for all its members. From the trash it comes back with its members for 30 days.

files.title: Files
files.intro: The Markdown files are the truth. Here: the index over them, the trash, and bringing in an Obsidian vault.

index.title: Index
index.text: nexlore watches the vault folder and reads every change, also those made by Obsidian, Syncthing or an editor. A full pass every few minutes catches what the watcher missed.
index.heldBack: Most files of {{spaces}} vanished at once. nexlore did not move them to the trash, because a folder that is not mounted looks just like that.

trash.title: Trash
trash.text: Deleted notes stay here for 30 days with their history, then they go for good. Notes deleted outside nexlore land here too.
trash.purgeText: This cannot be undone: the file and its history are gone.

import.title: Import an Obsidian vault
import.text: A ZIP of the vault becomes a new space. .obsidian and plugin syntax come along untouched; the report says what nexlore shows as code instead of running it.
import.name: Name of the new space

report.notUtf8: Files that are not UTF-8 text (read-only)
report.caseTwins: Names that differ only in case

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.text: Pictures and other files of the notes. Uploaded files land in a folder “{{folder}}” next to their note.
attachments.stripOn: place and device are removed from photos
attachments.none: No attachments in this space yet.
attachments.noneUnused: Every file here is used by a note.

editor.handleDrag: Drag to move, click to select

dates.hint: Enter: link to the daily note, Shift+Enter: the date alone

properties.title: Properties
properties.notYaml: The front matter is not a list of names and values, so it is edited as text here.
properties.name: Name
properties.duplicate: This name exists already; the row is not saved until it has a name of its own.

compare.title: Compare the note with the conflict copy
compare.equal: Both are the same. The copy can go.
compare.hint: The copy goes to the trash afterwards; it can come back from there for 30 days.
compare.keepNote: Keep the note, remove the copy

file.notFound: This file is not there (any more).
file.noPreview: No preview for this kind of file. Download it to open it.
file.deleteText: The file goes to the trash and can be restored there for 30 days.
file.deleteUsed_one: One note links this file; the link will point nowhere. The file can be restored from the trash for 30 days.
file.deleteUsed_other: {{count}} notes link this file; their links will point nowhere. The file can be restored from the trash for 30 days.

auth.name: Name
auth.nameHint: Small letters, digits, dots, dashes. You sign in with it.
auth.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.

login.title: Sign in
login.passwordOff: Signing in with a password is turned off here. Only the operator still can.

setup.title: Set up nexlore
setup.text: The account you make now is the operator's: it runs this server, invites others and sets things up.

invite.title: You are invited
invite.intoSpace: Into the space {{space}}, with the right to {{role}}.
invite.invalidText: It was used already, it ran out, or it was withdrawn. Ask for a new one.
invite.haveAccount: You are signed in as {{name}} and have an account already.

profile.name: Name
profile.hint: A photo from your phone or camera. It is cut to a square, and nothing of the file but the picture is kept: no place, no device.

account.title: My account
account.linked: Your account is linked to the provider.

password.title: Password
password.done: Password changed. Other browsers have to sign in again.

oidc.title: Sign-in provider
oidc.only: This account signs in through the provider.
oidc.linked: Linked: you can sign in with the provider as well as with your password.
oidc.text: Link your account to the provider, then you can sign in with either. Your password confirms it is you.

sessions.title: Other browsers
sessions.text: Signs you out everywhere except here, for example after losing a phone.
sessions.done: Every other browser is signed out.

members.title: Members of {{space}}
members.resetOnly: You do not read this space. As the operator you can change rights, not give yourself one.

invite.title: Invite
invite.text: A link to pass on. Whoever follows it makes an account, or joins with the one they have.
invite.once: The link works once. It is shown only now.

share.title: Public page
share.text: Anybody with the link can read it, without an account.
share.passwordHint: Readers have to give it once.
share.leaves: Only the text goes out: no properties, no %%comments%%. Links to notes that are not shared become plain text.

public.goneText: The link may have run out or been withdrawn.

css.title: Own CSS
css.text: Accounts may add CSS snippets for their own pages. Every snippet is read by a CSS parser; nothing that loads from elsewhere passes.
css.allowHint: Closed, no snippet reaches any page (they stay stored).

admin.title: Server
admin.text: Only you see this part, as the operator.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.text: Everybody who can sign in here.
accounts.locked: locked for a while after wrong passwords
accounts.passwordSet: Password set. The account was signed out everywhere.
accounts.operatorText: An operator sees every account and every setting, and can restore backups.
accounts.memberText: A member keeps the spaces and rights they have, without the settings of the server.
accounts.deleteText: Its rights go with it; its notes stay where they are. A space it was alone in becomes yours.
accounts.inviteText: Without a space: the new account makes its own spaces or is added to others later.
accounts.resetText: For a lost phone. The account is signed out everywhere and signs in with its password alone until it sets up a new one.
accounts.resetDone: Second factor reset. The account was signed out everywhere.

spaces.title: All spaces
spaces.text: Names and members only. You read a space only if you are in it or it has no members.
spaces.yours: no members, so it is yours

signIn.title: Sign-in
signIn.passwordHint: Off, only the provider lets members in. You as the operator can always use your password.
signIn.addressHint: The address people use to reach nexlore. Invitation links, public pages and the provider use it.
signIn.twoFactorHint: Every account that signs in with a password must set one up before it gets any further. Accounts from the provider bring its own.

oidc.title: OpenID Connect
oidc.secretKept: stored, leave empty to keep it
oidc.name: Name on the button
oidc.autoCreateHint: Off: only invited or linked accounts come in through the provider.

authentik.title: authentik in one step
authentik.text: With an API token that may create applications, nexlore sets up provider and application in authentik itself.

shares.title: Public pages
shares.text: Notes on the web without an account. Closed, every link answers as if it never existed.
shares.allowHint: Managers of a space may then share notes and folders.

mail.title: Invitation mail
mail.text: Without a server nothing is sent; the link to copy is enough.

files.title: Files
files.text: Where uploads go and how much they may take.
files.strip: Remove place and device from photos
files.stripHint: On upload, from pictures and videos. The picture itself stays as it is.

backups.title: Backups
backups.text: Notes, files, the trash and the database in one archive.
backups.downloadText: The archive is not encrypted: it holds every note and the key of the server. Enter your password once more.
backups.usable: The archive is complete and readable.
backups.damaged: The archive is damaged. It cannot be restored.
backups.would: A restore would add {{add}}, change {{change}} and remove {{remove}} files.
backups.restoreText: The current state is backed up first. nexlore then restarts, and everybody signs in again.
backups.restarting: nexlore restarts with the backup. Sign in again in a moment.

languages.title: Languages
languages.text: Your own translations, from the template under Language.

mcp.title: AI from outside (MCP)
mcp.text: Off by default. Switched on, every account makes keys of its own; a key never sees more than its account.
mcp.allowHint: Programs outside reach notes with a key per account.
mcp.maxLevel: Highest level a key may have
mcp.keysWhere: Keys are made by every account for itself, under My account → AI from outside, with the lines to paste into a program.
mcp.keysLater: Once it is on, every account makes its keys under My account.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.text: From the checked catalog that comes with nexlore. Installed means off for everybody until you let it out; then everybody switches it on for themselves.
plugins.uploadAllow: Allow plugin files of one's own
plugins.uploadHint: Not checked by anybody; they run just as locked up.
plugins.warnShort: Code nobody checked: through WebRTC it could send the notes it is shown to somewhere else.
plugins.warnText: A plugin file of your own is code nobody has checked. It runs locked up in its frame and cannot reach nexlore by itself, but browsers do not let nexlore block every way out: through WebRTC such a plugin could send what it is shown (the note it runs on, and what it may read) to somewhere else. Allow only files whose code you have read, or whose author you trust.
plugins.uploadText: Once you let it out, this plugin runs for everybody who switches it on. Through WebRTC it could send the notes it is shown to somewhere else. Upload only code you have read, or whose author you trust.
plugins.nextStep: Let out: every account can now switch it on for itself under My account → Plugins for me.

ai.title: AI in notes
ai.text: Every account may connect its own AI service and use it in the editor. The text a person chooses leaves the server for that service.
ai.allowHint: Off: nothing goes out, and the editor offers no AI. Accounts keep their access for later.
ai.where: Each account sets up its service under My account → AI in notes.

guide.title: The guide
guide.text: The space “nexlore” explains nexlore with notes that use what they explain. It is made at the first start; here it is made again, next to what is there. Nothing is overwritten.

today.title: Open today's daily note (Alt+T)
today.none: There is no space you may write in.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.hint: Click a day to open its daily note, or to make it from the template.
calendar.readOnly: You may only read in this space: a daily note that is not there cannot be made.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.hint: Tasks from every space you may read. Ticking one off writes only its line into the note.
tasks.conflict: The note was changed elsewhere meanwhile: your tick went into a conflict copy.
tasks.changed: This task changed in its note meanwhile. The list was loaded again.
tasks.noneYet: No tasks yet. Any line like this in a note is one:
tasks.noneYetMore: The date is optional; ticking it off here writes the line in the note.

newNote.title: New note in “{{folder}}”
newNote.name: Title
newNote.noTemplates: This space has no templates yet. Notes in its templates folder become templates.
newNote.preview: Preview, with the placeholders filled in
newNote.templater: Templater commands are never run; they stay in the note as text.
newNote.placeholders: A template is a note in the templates folder. In it, {{title}}, {{date}}, {{time}} and {{date:DD.MM.YYYY}} are filled in when a note is made from it.

spaceOptions.themeHint: Only the notes of the space wear it; the sidebar and the header stay in each reader’s own theme. Readers may switch it off.
spaceOptions.title: Options of “{{space}}”
spaceOptions.text: For everybody who writes in this space. A daily note is always named YYYY-MM-DD.md.
spaceOptions.rootHint: Empty: right in the space; then every note named like a date counts as a daily note.

install.title: nexlore as an app on your home screen
install.text: A window and an icon of its own. It needs a connection to the server.
install.ios: In Safari, tap “Share”, then “Add to Home Screen”.

mcp.title: AI from outside (MCP)
mcp.text: AI programs on your computer, or an agent, read your notes with a key. They see only what you may read yourself.
mcp.name: Name
mcp.allSpaces: All spaces I may read, later ones too
mcp.shownOnce: Key “{{name}}” made. It is shown only now.

levelText.read: Search, read notes, links and tasks. Nothing is changed.
levelText.draft: Also proposals, which you take over or throw away on the note.
levelText.write: Changes notes directly: every change a version, a conflict copy when the note changed in the meantime.

mcp.off: The operator has not switched on AI from outside, so there are no keys to make here.
mcp.offOperator: Switch it on under Settings → Server → AI and plugins.
mcp.nextStep: Next: give your AI program the address and the key. Programs that read an mcp.json (Cursor, for example, or a project’s .mcp.json) take the JSON below; Claude Code takes the command. Others ask for the same two things in their own settings. The key works until you revoke it.
mcp.howToText: The key was shown only once. Put it where it says YOUR-KEY, or make a new key.

drafts.changedSince: The note changed since the AI read it. Taking it over writes a conflict copy, nothing is overwritten.

plugins.mineText: The operator let these out; you switch them on for yourself. Each runs locked up: no network, no sign-in, only what it lists here.

permission.note_read: read the note it sits on
permission.note_write: write the note it sits on

where.panel: Shows beside every note in the tab “Plugins”.
where.block: Write a code block ```{{lang}} into a note: when the note is read, the plugin shows its result in its place.
where.view: A note with the property “{{key}}” shows this view instead of its text when read; a switch leads back to the text.

twofactor.title: Second factor
twofactor.lead: Besides the password, a code from an app on your phone (any authenticator app that takes a QR code). Recovery codes on paper get you in when the phone is gone.
twofactor.provider: You sign in through the provider; its second factor applies.
twofactor.scan: Scan this code with the app, or type the key below into it. Then give the code the app shows, and your password.
twofactor.qr: QR code for the authenticator app
twofactor.codeHint: Six digits. Or one of your recovery codes.
twofactor.passwordHint: Proves it is you at the keyboard.
twofactor.codesLead: Each one signs you in once, when the phone is not at hand. They are shown only now: copy them or save them as a file, and keep them apart from the phone.
twofactor.renewText: The old recovery codes stop working. Give your password to make new ones.
twofactor.disableText: From then on the password alone signs you in. Give it to turn the second factor off.
twofactor.lowCodes: Few recovery codes left. Make new ones while you can still sign in.
twofactor.loginText: The code from your app, or a recovery code.
twofactor.requiredText: The operator requires a second factor for every account that signs in with a password. Set it up to go on.

actions.name: Name
actions.renameHint: Links to it in other notes follow, in every space.
actions.moveHint: Into a folder of the same space. Links to it follow.
actions.trashFolderTitle: Move the folder “{{name}}” to the trash?
actions.trashFolderText: With every note and file in it. It all stays in the trash for 30 days and comes back from the Files page.
actions.newSpaceHint: A folder at the top of the vault. You manage it and can invite others; nobody else sees it until then.
actions.asTemplateText: A copy goes into the templates folder of the space and shows up under “New note”. The note itself stays as it is.
actions.asTemplateFailed: The template could not be saved.

looks.title: Symbol and colour for “{{name}}”
looks.hint: Everybody in the space sees it so, in the sidebar and on the map. A folder’s colour holds for the folders in it too.
looks.notSaved: The symbol and colour could not be saved; try again from the context menu.
looks.search: Search {{count}} more symbols, in English or German
looks.none: No symbol matches. Try an English word.
looks.lucide: More symbols from Lucide (lucide.dev, ISC licence).

find.label: Find in the note
find.commandReplace: Find and replace in the note

unlinked.title: Unlinked mentions
unlinked.none: No other note names this one without a link.
unlinked.loadFailed: The mentions could not be loaded.
unlinked.readOnly: You may only read in this space.
unlinked.locked: Someone is editing that note right now.
unlinked.more: There are more places; the first 200 are shown.

cleanup.intro: What lies about loose in a space: notes without any link, and links with nothing behind them.
cleanup.lonelyText: No link leads to them and none away. "Mentions" shows where other notes name them.
cleanup.lonelyNone: Every note hangs on at least one link.
cleanup.brokenText: These links name a note or file that is not there. "Create" makes the note where a click on the link would.

capture.title: Quick capture
capture.placeholder: A thought, a link, a task …
capture.noSpace: There is no space you may write in.
capture.locked: Someone is editing the inbox. Try again in a moment.

feed.title: Calendar subscription
feed.text: Your open tasks with a date as an address your calendar subscribes to (internet calendar, ICS). It asks for it again about every hour.
feed.closed: The operator has not switched calendar subscriptions on.
feed.closedOperator: Switch them on under Settings → Server → Extensions.
feed.active: An address is active. It is shown only once; a new one replaces it.
feed.shownOnce: Visible only now. Whoever has this address sees your tasks with a date.
feed.adminText: Every account can make an address for its calendar, with its open tasks that have a date. The tasks leave the house that way.
feed.allowHint: Switched off, every address answers as if it did not exist.

log.title: Log
log.text: The newest lines of the server's log. Passwords, keys and note texts are never in it.
log.clearText: Every line goes, the older files too.

comments.title: Comments
comments.none: No comments yet. Choose words in the reading view and pick "Comment".
comments.reveal: To the place in the text
comments.gone: The words are no longer in the text.

viewer.title: Picture
viewer.fromWeb: A picture from the web: view only

ai.title: AI in notes
ai.text: Your own AI service corrects, rewrites, translates, summarizes and writes in the editor. You pay for its key yourself; a result is always shown next to the text first and changes nothing until you take it over.
ai.off: The operator has not switched on AI in notes.
ai.offOperator: Switch it on under Settings → Server → AI and plugins.
ai.tiles: Fill in the address of a service
ai.address: Address (any service that speaks the usual chat interface)
ai.keyNone: none (a service at home may need none)
ai.modelsFound_one: {{count}} model found: address and key are right.
ai.modelsFound_other: {{count}} models found: address and key are right.
ai.switchHint: The editor then shows “AI” in its toolbar and in its menu.
ai.switchIncomplete: Save an address and a model first.
ai.whereItGoes: The text you choose goes to the address above, nothing else. What happens to it there is up to that service and its conditions.
ai.eventsText: Every request to your service, word for word, 14 days long. Shown as text, never as a page.
ai.writePlaceholder: An agenda for Thursday’s meeting, from the points in this note
ai.writeMaterial: The note (or the selection) goes along as material.
ai.tooShort: Select a few words first, or write some into the note.
ai.untouched: The note is unchanged. The proposal replaces the selection only when you take it over.
ai.taken: Taken over. Undo brings the old text back.
ai.untouchedNote: The note is unchanged. The proposal replaces its text only when you take it over.

start.title: Start page
start.text: Where nexlore opens for you, on every device. The map stays one click away.
